item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-cd01ad337d811492","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"On 16 December 2023, SADC launched an observation mission for the DRC’s 20 December presidential, legislative, and provincial elections under its revised 2021 democratic-election principles and guidelines, intended to identify procedural deficiencies and strengthen democratic practice.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 election period under Tshisekedi’s presidency.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes the election process and the regional observation mission but does not attribute the mission’s launch personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The excerpt does not report the mission’s findings or whether identified deficiencies were remedied."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e2c7f1e2300ec5d3","start_unit":12,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The DRC submitted its declaration under Article 2 of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons on 25 April 2023.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.4","1B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The declaration date falls within 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source records a state action during Tshisekedi’s presidency but does not identify the president or domestic decision process responsible.","limitations":["The excerpt gives no text of the declaration, implementation measures, verification arrangements, or evidence of Tshisekedi’s personal role."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8e31e7646c395b69","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In response to displacement caused by clashes between the Congolese army and M23 in eastern DRC, the ICRC distributed food to 47,280 displaced people and host-family members at Kanyaruchinya, 670 people in Goma, and cash assistance to 44,910 people where access and security problems hindered in-kind aid.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The article was published 12 January 2023 and reports assistance delivered at the end of December 2022, providing context at the start of the target year rather than a 2023 government result.","ruler_attribution":"The assistance was delivered by the ICRC with the DRC Red Cross; the source does not attribute the response to Tshisekedi or the central government.","limitations":["The source reports humanitarian action by the ICRC, not a Tshisekedi-directed or state-funded program.","It also reports unsanitary shelter conditions, cholera cases, low household incomes, and continuing access constraints."]},{"source_id":"SRC-01412f97ade43106","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported that the STEP social-protection program, implemented by the DRC Social Fund with the Ministry of Social Affairs and other partners, had benefited over 5.8 million people, including 3 million women; provided safety-net support to 530,000 people totaling $93 million; and upgraded 2,185 community infrastructures in 1,166 vulnerable communities between February 2014 and December 2022.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.9","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Results end in December 2022 and are reported in February 2023; they are inherited or ongoing program results rather than clearly new 2023 outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The program was implemented through DRC public institutions, but the excerpt does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal direction or the share of results attributable to his administration.","limitations":["The program was substantially donor-funded and began before Tshisekedi’s 2023 period.","The source does not provide independent outcome evaluation, distributional incidence beyond sex and community targeting, or evidence of central-government financing."]},{"source_id":"SRC-01412f97ade43106","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The STEP institutional arrangement placed policy responsibility with the Ministry of Social Affairs while delegating safety-net execution to a technical public agency; the World Bank said this supported a balance between long-term system-building and delivery, with efforts underway to develop a multi-donor/government-funded national safety-net system.","question_ids":["6B.4","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The institutional assessment is reported in February 2023 and describes a system developed through December 2022 with planned continuation.","ruler_attribution":"The arrangement involves DRC government institutions, but the source does not attribute its design or adaptation to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The national safety-net system remained a future objective; the excerpt does not establish durable government funding or completed transition from donor dependence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0ce588bb01ffab46","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"A government-released IPC analysis reported that 25.8 million people in the DRC faced crisis or emergency food insecurity, while 6.7 million in North and South Kivu and Ituri experienced crisis or emergency levels, a 10 percent increase from the previous year; causes included poor harvests, conflict displacement, disease, unemployment, and collapsing infrastructure.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","5B.9","6B.2","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures were reported on 30 May 2023 and concern the 2023 food-security situation.","ruler_attribution":"The analysis was released by the government, but the source does not establish that Tshisekedi caused the conditions or specify his personal policy response.","limitations":["The report identifies multiple structural and external causes, so it does not isolate presidential responsibility.","The excerpt reports humanitarian and agricultural agencies’ planned responses but not completed central-government corrective action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1962d3de1c368f16","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"On 28 June 2023, at least 12 FARDC soldiers arrested and beat three journalists covering a Kinshasa land dispute; the journalists were detained at a DEMIAP intelligence office and released without charges after interventions by the UN mission and others. CPJ called for accountability and described repeated attacks by security forces as an alarming pattern.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The arrests and beatings occurred during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The perpetrators were FARDC soldiers and the detention site was a DEMIAP office; the source does not show that Tshisekedi personally ordered the abuse or that authorities under him investigated or punished those responsible.","limitations":["The excerpt provides no confirmed presidential response or final accountability outcome.","A FARDC spokesperson disputed the journalists’ account, claiming they had attacked soldiers."]},{"source_id":"SRC-82a8691bf56b4460","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International reported that M23 fighters summarily killed at least 20 men and raped at least 66 women and girls in eastern DRC between 21 and 30 November 2022; survivors lacked adequate medical and mental-health assistance, and nearly three months later there had been minimal progress by Congolese authorities in investigating the crimes or holding perpetrators accountable.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.10","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The crimes occurred in late 2022, while the reported lack of official investigative progress was assessed in February 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source records Congolese authorities’ condemnation and promise to pursue justice but does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal involvement or responsibility for M23 conduct.","limitations":["The abuses were attributed to M23, described as Rwandan-backed, rather than to state forces.","The excerpt does not report later investigations, prosecutions, or remedial measures after the publication date."]},{"source_id":"SRC-eee9e3686e17cb0d","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A World Bank study informed the review of the DRC education strategy through a gender lens and led to a Girls’ Learning and Empowerment Project and a $135 million Global Partnership for Education compact; the planned project targeted safe and equitable secondary education, scholarships in the lowest-enrollment province, improved materials and teaching, and protection from sexual abuse, exploitation, and harassment.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The results brief was published in May 2023 and describes policy development during the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The project was prepared by the DRC Ministry of Primary, Secondary, and Technical Education and publicly endorsed by a finance minister, but the excerpt does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal role.","limitations":["The source mainly reports analytical work, project design, and funding commitments; it does not demonstrate completed implementation or outcomes in 2023.","The baseline data cited for gender gaps and violence precede the target year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-eee9e3686e17cb0d","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The study found substantial pre-existing gender disparities: 33 of every 100 girls aged 14–17 were out of school, rural girls were 23 percentage points less likely than rural boys and 46 points less likely than urban boys to enter grade 12, and surveyed girls faced significant physical and sexual violence risks.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence uses 2013–14 and 2017–18 surveys and therefore establishes baseline conditions relevant to 2023, not a new 2023 outcome.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern national conditions inherited by the administration; they do not attribute the disparities to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The cited surveys predate 2023 and cannot establish change during Tshisekedi’s target period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0ed19e56e33696b4","start_unit":20,"end_unit":22,"fact_summary":"In April 2023, ANR agents arrested journalist Gustave Bakuka over an article described as spreading false rumors; a prosecutor detained journalist Diègo Kayiba over tweets criticizing a public official; an elected representative threatened journalist Sylvain Kabongo with arrest; and ANR agents had separately arrested journalist John Ngongo Lomango over security reporting and retained his phone after release.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"All principal incidents described occurred in March–April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct involved ANR agents, a prosecutor, and an elected representative; the source does not establish a direct order from Tshisekedi or a presidential response.","limitations":["The source does not report final judicial outcomes or whether the administration corrected the practices.","The article is a CPJ account based partly on confidential sources and reviewed material."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e7f96729972ff820","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"ACLED reported that the December 2023 election period, which resulted in Tshisekedi’s second term, saw violence targeting civilians rise 54 percent from November; political-party-linked gunmen and rioters targeted party supporters, journalists, and CENI election workers, with violence continuing after polls closed and eastern provinces remaining heavily affected.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.7","2B.10","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","4B.1","4B.3","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns December 2023 and the election producing Tshisekedi’s second term.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies violence by unidentified gunmen and political-party-associated rioters and does not establish that Tshisekedi ordered or directly controlled the attacks.","limitations":["The excerpt does not assess the credibility of the election result, identify perpetrators individually, or report official investigations or remedies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8f2b6ad87756bc01","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"A January 2023 poll found that 54 percent of respondents might not vote in the scheduled presidential election, only 37 percent believed CENI could organize credible, free, and transparent elections, and low turnout appeared likely to favor Tshisekedi, with a projected 50.42 percent of votes cast; the researchers warned that record abstention could weaken the eventual winner’s legitimacy.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.6","4B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The poll was conducted in mid-January 2023 regarding the December 2023 election.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern electoral conditions that could benefit Tshisekedi but do not prove that he caused low turnout or manipulated CENI.","limitations":["These were prospective polling estimates, not observed election results.","The excerpt does not establish presidential control over CENI or subsequent corrective action."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-3f321c92e9173bbc"],"batch_limitations":["Several sources describe actions by international organizations, donors, public agencies, security forces, or armed groups without establishing Félix Tshisekedi’s personal direction, responsibility, or corrective response.","Evidence from late 2022 and earlier surveys is included only where it materially establishes baseline conditions or institutional continuity relevant to the 2023 period."]}
